1.name: MOP

fields.name: mop_type
fields.meaning: Template selector: 0 uses instruction count/mask fields with configuration; 1 takes the loop structure from configuration.

fields.name: loop_count
fields.meaning: Template-0 Count1 field; ignored by the template-1 repository usage.

fields.name: zmask_lo16_or_loop_count
fields.meaning: Template-0 low zero-mask/count payload, depending on template configuration. Ordinary template-1 calls pass zero.

1.title: Execute a configured macro-op
1.summary: Expand a configured macro-op template into ordinary Tensix instructions.
notes: The repository programs template words first, then executes TTMOP(1, 0, 0). MOP, REPLAY and SFPLOADMACRO are three different mechanisms.

2.name: NOP
2.title: Tensix no operation
2.summary: Issue a frontend no-op, useful as a harmless instruction in MOP/replay templates or as spacing.
notes: TTNOP, TTSFPNOP and TTDMANOP target different instruction paths. None is a universal completion barrier.

4.name: REPLAY

fields.name: start_idx
fields.meaning: First replay-buffer slot. The Python encoder exposes ten bits; actual buffer capacity is architecture-specific.

fields.name: len
fields.meaning: Number of instructions to record or replay. This is a sequence length, not a repeat count.

fields.name: execute_while_loading
fields.meaning: 0 records without execution; 1 also executes during recording. Other values in the wider encoder field are not documented ordinary modes.

fields.name: load_mode
fields.meaning: 1 records incoming instructions; 0 replays stored instructions.

4.title: Record or replay instructions
4.summary: Store a sequence in the thread's replay buffer, optionally executing while recording, or expand a previously recorded sequence.
notes: Recording consumes the next len Tensix words. A later replay expands the stored words once; repetition comes from a MOP or software loop.

The available shared manual describes the Wormhole buffer size and field widths. Do not carry its 32-slot capacity or count-zero behavior over to Blackhole. Use the Blackhole replay helper limits and the retained replay_fifo_probe when exploring capacity.

8.name: MOVD2A

fields.name: dest_32b_lo
fields.meaning: Select the low half of a 32-bit Dst datum before conversion; normally zero.

fields.name: src
fields.meaning: SrcA destination row offset added to its RWC.

fields.name: addr_mode
fields.meaning: Raw address-modifier field. Selects preconfigured counter updates after the instruction, not a byte stride. The Python bit field is wider than the semantic selector; do not assume every encodable value is valid.

fields.name: instr_mod
fields.meaning: 0 moves one row; 2 moves four rows, rounding both row addresses down to multiples of four.

fields.name: dst
fields.meaning: Dst row offset added to the math target offset, Dst RWC and configured Dst base, then aligned for the instruction footprint. This is not an L1 byte address.

8.title: Move Dst to SrcA
8.summary: Move one row or an aligned four-row block from Dst to SrcA, with configured format conversion.
notes: Dst is the source despite the Python dst argument name. Src row is the destination.
MOVD2B uses the SrcA format configuration to derive SrcB style; the shared manual explicitly calls out this behavior.

10.name: MOVD2B

fields.name: dest_32b_lo
fields.meaning: Select the low half of a 32-bit Dst datum before conversion; normally zero.

fields.name: src
fields.meaning: SrcB destination row offset added to its RWC.

fields.name: addr_mode
fields.meaning: Raw address-modifier field. Selects preconfigured counter updates after the instruction, not a byte stride. The Python bit field is wider than the semantic selector; do not assume every encodable value is valid.

fields.name: instr_mod
fields.meaning: 0 moves one row; 2 moves four rows, rounding both row addresses down to multiples of four.

fields.name: dst
fields.meaning: Dst row offset added to the math target offset, Dst RWC and configured Dst base, then aligned for the instruction footprint. This is not an L1 byte address.

10.title: Move Dst to SrcB
10.summary: Move one row or an aligned four-row block from Dst to SrcB, with configured format conversion.
notes: Dst is the source despite the Python dst argument name. Src row is the destination.
MOVD2B uses the SrcA format configuration to derive SrcB style; the shared manual explicitly calls out this behavior.

11.name: MOVB2A

fields.name: srca
fields.meaning: SrcA destination row offset added to its RWC.

fields.name: addr_mode
fields.meaning: Raw address-modifier field. Selects preconfigured counter updates after the instruction, not a byte stride. The Python bit field is wider than the semantic selector; do not assume every encodable value is valid.

fields.name: instr_mod
fields.meaning: 0 moves one row; 2 moves four rows aligned to multiples of four.

fields.name: srcb
fields.meaning: SrcB source row offset added to its RWC.

11.title: Move SrcB to SrcA
11.summary: Copy one row or an aligned four-row block from SrcB to SrcA.
notes: Automatically waits for SrcB ownership, but does not automatically wait for SrcA ownership.

16.name: ZEROACC

fields.name: clear_mode
fields.meaning: Raw five-bit field in isa.py. The shared manual places Mode in bits 20:19 and UseDst32b in bit 21, so these semantic fields fall within this Python argument.

fields.name: use_32_bit_mode
fields.meaning: Encoder bit 18. Despite this name, the shared manual labels bit 18 Revert, not UseDst32b. Treat nonzero use as an unresolved encoder/manual discrepancy.

fields.name: clear_zero_flags
fields.meaning: Encoder bit 17; not documented as a public operand in the shared ZEROACC syntax. Keep zero unless separately verified.

fields.name: addr_mode
fields.meaning: Raw address-modifier field. Selects preconfigured counter updates after the instruction, not a byte stride. The Python bit field is wider than the semantic selector; do not assume every encodable value is valid.

fields.name: where
fields.meaning: Mode-dependent row/block selection. In the shared model: mode 0 selects an offset row, 1 selects a 16-row block, 2 a Dst half, 3 all Dst. Do not translate existing Python calls using argument names alone.

16.title: Invalidate accumulator rows
16.summary: Mark Dst rows undefined so later FPU accumulation reads an identity value, and packer reads produce zeros.
notes: Important source mismatch: the Python wrapper and shared ISA diagram disagree on operand naming and placement. Existing calls use TTZEROACC(3, 1, 0, 1, ...); this page preserves them without claiming the shared model explains that combination. A focused hardware probe is required before changing this encoding.
ZEROACC does not physically fill Dst with zeros. SFPU loads from undefined rows are undefined, and partial SFPU/unpacker writes to such rows are also unsafe.

17.name: ZEROSRC

fields.name: zero_val
fields.meaning: 0 writes zero; the documented low-bit option writes negative infinity to SrcA. The wider encoder field is not a general fill immediate.

fields.name: write_mode
fields.meaning: For a single-bank clear: 1 selects the math-owned bank; 0 selects the unpacker-owned bank.

fields.name: bank_mask
fields.meaning: 1 clears both banks; 0 clears one bank selected by write_mode.

fields.name: src_mask
fields.meaning: Bitmask: 1 SrcA, 2 SrcB, 3 both.

17.title: Clear source register banks
17.summary: Clear all rows of selected SrcA/SrcB banks to zero, with an optional negative-infinity value for SrcA.
notes: Clearing source storage and transferring source-bank ownership are separate actions. Synchronize before clearing a bank still used by another unit.

18.name: MOVA2D

fields.name: dest_32b_lo
fields.meaning: Low-half Dst write selector. Keep 0 for the normal FP32 path. UseDst32bLo with a TF32-style move can corrupt data on Blackhole (TEN-4245).

fields.name: src
fields.meaning: SrcA row offset added to its RWC.

fields.name: addr_mode
fields.meaning: Raw address-modifier field. Selects preconfigured counter updates after the instruction, not a byte stride. The Python bit field is wider than the semantic selector; do not assume every encodable value is valid.

fields.name: instr_mod
fields.meaning: 0 moves one row; 2 moves an aligned eight-row block.

fields.name: dst
fields.meaning: Dst row offset added to the math target offset, Dst RWC and configured Dst base, then aligned for the instruction footprint. This is not an L1 byte address.

18.title: Move SrcA to Dst
18.summary: Transfer rows from SrcA into Dst, with format handling determined by the math configuration.
notes: Blackhole FP32 accumulation causes source-to-Dst moves to write FP32 Dst values. Wait before consuming the affected Dst rows with SFPU.

19.name: MOVB2D

fields.name: dest_32b_lo
fields.meaning: Low-half Dst write selector. Keep 0 for the normal FP32 path. UseDst32bLo with a TF32-style move can corrupt data on Blackhole (TEN-4245).

fields.name: src
fields.meaning: SrcB row offset added to its RWC.

fields.name: addr_mode
fields.meaning: Raw address-modifier field. Selects preconfigured counter updates after the instruction, not a byte stride. The Python bit field is wider than the semantic selector; do not assume every encodable value is valid.

fields.name: movb2d_instr_mod
fields.meaning: Bit flags: 1 broadcasts column 0; 2 broadcasts one row to eight Dst rows; 4 moves an aligned four-row block.

fields.name: dst
fields.meaning: Dst row offset added to the math target offset, Dst RWC and configured Dst base, then aligned for the instruction footprint. This is not an L1 byte address.

19.title: Move SrcB to Dst
19.summary: Transfer rows from SrcB into Dst, with format handling determined by the math configuration.
notes: Blackhole FP32 accumulation causes source-to-Dst moves to write FP32 Dst values. Wait before consuming the affected Dst rows with SFPU.

22.name: TRNSPSRCB
22.title: Transpose SrcB rows 16–31
22.summary: Transpose the 16 × 16 matrix in rows 16 through 31 of the current SrcB bank.
notes: Waits for the FPU to own SrcB. No row or tile selector is encoded.

38.name: MVMUL

fields.name: clear_dvalid
fields.meaning: Source-bank release mask: 0 keeps both, 1 flips/releases SrcA, 2 SrcB, 3 both. Release hands the consumed bank back to the unpacker unless clearing is disabled in configuration.

fields.name: instr_mod19
fields.meaning: Normal mode is 0. The documented low-bit mode broadcasts one SrcB row to alternating output rows; this is not ordinary eight-row broadcast.

fields.name: addr_mode
fields.meaning: Raw address-modifier field. Selects preconfigured counter updates after the instruction, not a byte stride. The Python bit field is wider than the semantic selector; do not assume every encodable value is valid.

fields.name: dst
fields.meaning: Dst row offset added to the math target offset, Dst RWC and configured Dst base, then aligned for the instruction footprint. This is not an L1 byte address.

38.title: Matrix multiply-accumulate
38.summary: Compute Dst[8 x 16] += SrcB[8 x 16] @ SrcA[16 x 16]. A full 32 x 32 tile operation is a sequence of these instructions.
notes: Always accumulates. Initialize Dst first if an assignment is intended. Multipliers consume partial mantissas; choose and schedule the required fidelity phases.

The retained Blackhole FPU test report observes that SrcA starts round down to an even 128-element slot. Use aligned 16-row A pairs. This is stricter than the current shared manual's A-row mask; tests/compute/fpu/README.md records the discrepancy.

39.name: ELWMUL

fields.name: clear_dvalid
fields.meaning: Source-bank release mask: 0 keeps both, 1 flips/releases SrcA, 2 SrcB, 3 both. Release hands the consumed bank back to the unpacker unless clearing is disabled in configuration.

fields.name: dest_accum_en
fields.meaning: 0 overwrites Dst with the result; 1 adds the result to existing Dst.

fields.name: instr_mod19
fields.meaning: SrcB broadcast: 0 none; 1 column 0; 2 one row; 3 one scalar (row plus column broadcast).

fields.name: addr_mode
fields.meaning: Raw address-modifier field. Selects preconfigured counter updates after the instruction, not a byte stride. The Python bit field is wider than the semantic selector; do not assume every encodable value is valid.

fields.name: dst
fields.meaning: Dst row offset added to the math target offset, Dst RWC and configured Dst base, then aligned for the instruction footprint. This is not an L1 byte address.

39.title: Elementwise multiplication
39.summary: Multiply aligned 8 x 16 blocks from SrcA and SrcB, optionally accumulating into Dst over fidelity phases.
notes: Data formats and FP32 accumulation are configured separately. Source-bank ownership must permit math to read both sources.
Multiplication precision depends on fidelity phases. The retained HiFi2 tests issue phase 0 for all output blocks, then phase 1. ELWADD/ELWSUB require fidelity phase zero.

40.name: ELWADD

fields.name: clear_dvalid
fields.meaning: Source-bank release mask: 0 keeps both, 1 flips/releases SrcA, 2 SrcB, 3 both. Release hands the consumed bank back to the unpacker unless clearing is disabled in configuration.

fields.name: dest_accum_en
fields.meaning: 0 overwrites Dst with the result; 1 adds the result to existing Dst.

fields.name: instr_mod19
fields.meaning: SrcB broadcast: 0 none; 1 column 0; 2 one row; 3 one scalar (row plus column broadcast).

fields.name: addr_mode
fields.meaning: Raw address-modifier field. Selects preconfigured counter updates after the instruction, not a byte stride. The Python bit field is wider than the semantic selector; do not assume every encodable value is valid.

fields.name: dst
fields.meaning: Dst row offset added to the math target offset, Dst RWC and configured Dst base, then aligned for the instruction footprint. This is not an L1 byte address.

40.title: Elementwise addition
40.summary: Add aligned 8 x 16 blocks from SrcA and SrcB, optionally accumulating into Dst.
notes: Data formats and FP32 accumulation are configured separately. Source-bank ownership must permit math to read both sources.
Multiplication precision depends on fidelity phases. The retained HiFi2 tests issue phase 0 for all output blocks, then phase 1. ELWADD/ELWSUB require fidelity phase zero.

48.name: ELWSUB

fields.name: clear_dvalid
fields.meaning: Source-bank release mask: 0 keeps both, 1 flips/releases SrcA, 2 SrcB, 3 both. Release hands the consumed bank back to the unpacker unless clearing is disabled in configuration.

fields.name: dest_accum_en
fields.meaning: 0 overwrites Dst with the result; 1 adds the result to existing Dst.

fields.name: instr_mod19
fields.meaning: SrcB broadcast: 0 none; 1 column 0; 2 one row; 3 one scalar (row plus column broadcast).

fields.name: addr_mode
fields.meaning: Raw address-modifier field. Selects preconfigured counter updates after the instruction, not a byte stride. The Python bit field is wider than the semantic selector; do not assume every encodable value is valid.

fields.name: dst
fields.meaning: Dst row offset added to the math target offset, Dst RWC and configured Dst base, then aligned for the instruction footprint. This is not an L1 byte address.

48.title: Elementwise subtraction
48.summary: Subtract aligned SrcB values from SrcA, optionally accumulating into Dst.
notes: Data formats and FP32 accumulation are configured separately. Source-bank ownership must permit math to read both sources.
Multiplication precision depends on fidelity phases. The retained HiFi2 tests issue phase 0 for all output blocks, then phase 1. ELWADD/ELWSUB require fidelity phase zero.

51.name: GMPOOL

fields.name: clear_dvalid
fields.meaning: Source-bank release mask: 0 keeps both, 1 flips/releases SrcA, 2 SrcB, 3 both. Release hands the consumed bank back to the unpacker unless clearing is disabled in configuration.

fields.name: instr_mod19
fields.meaning: Keep zero for the documented operation. The Python encoder exposes these bits, but they are not an independent supported operand in the reference syntax.

fields.name: pool_addr_mode
fields.meaning: Raw address-modifier field. Selects preconfigured counter updates after the instruction, not a byte stride. The Python bit field is wider than the semantic selector; do not assume every encodable value is valid.

fields.name: max_pool_index_en
fields.meaning: Keep 0 for the repository's non-index reduction. Index output is a separate mode requiring additional configuration.

fields.name: dst
fields.meaning: Dst row offset added to the math target offset, Dst RWC and configured Dst base, then aligned for the instruction footprint. This is not an L1 byte address.

51.title: Column-wise maximum reduction
51.summary: Reduce SrcA rows to a maximum per column, combine with the first Dst row, and clear the next three Dst rows in the normal non-index mode.
notes: SrcA uses an aligned 16 x 16 footprint. SrcB begins at an eight-row boundary. GAPOOL reads four SrcB rows; GMPOOL uses one row for exponent scaling (the tests use B=1).
The allocator reserves a 128-element Dst slot even though these instructions write fewer rows. Do not assume the unused rows are overwritten.

52.name: GAPOOL

fields.name: clear_dvalid
fields.meaning: Source-bank release mask: 0 keeps both, 1 flips/releases SrcA, 2 SrcB, 3 both. Release hands the consumed bank back to the unpacker unless clearing is disabled in configuration.

fields.name: instr_mod19
fields.meaning: Keep zero for the documented operation. The Python encoder exposes these bits, but they are not an independent supported operand in the reference syntax.

fields.name: pool_addr_mode
fields.meaning: Raw address-modifier field. Selects preconfigured counter updates after the instruction, not a byte stride. The Python bit field is wider than the semantic selector; do not assume every encodable value is valid.

fields.name: max_pool_index_en
fields.meaning: Keep 0 for the repository's non-index reduction. Index output is a separate mode requiring additional configuration.

fields.name: dst
fields.meaning: Dst row offset added to the math target offset, Dst RWC and configured Dst base, then aligned for the instruction footprint. This is not an L1 byte address.

52.title: Four-row weighted reduction
52.summary: Compute Dst[4 x 16] += SrcB[4 x 16] @ SrcA[16 x 16]. This is weighted summation, not an automatic mean.
notes: SrcA uses an aligned 16 x 16 footprint. SrcB begins at an eight-row boundary. GAPOOL reads four SrcB rows; GMPOOL uses one row for exponent scaling (the tests use B=1).
The allocator reserves a 128-element Dst slot even though these instructions write fewer rows. Do not assume the unused rows are overwritten.

53.name: GATESRCRST

fields.name: reset_srcb_gate_control
fields.meaning: 1 invalidates the SrcB operand cache.

fields.name: reset_srca_gate_control
fields.meaning: Keep zero for the documented operation. The Python encoder exposes these bits, but they are not an independent supported operand in the reference syntax.

53.title: Invalidate the SrcB operand cache
53.summary: Forcibly invalidate the one-slot SrcB operand cache feeding the FPU.
notes: This is cache invalidation, not source-bank ownership transfer.

54.name: CLEARDVALID

fields.name: cleardvalid
fields.meaning: Source-bank release mask: 0 keeps both, 1 flips/releases SrcA, 2 SrcB, 3 both. Release hands the consumed bank back to the unpacker unless clearing is disabled in configuration.

fields.name: reset
fields.meaning: Packed low bits: bit 0 resets source synchronization; bit 1 keeps reading the same bank after release. The remaining encoder bits are not public operands.

54.title: Release source banks to unpackers
54.summary: Release the selected SrcA/SrcB banks and optionally switch which banks the FPU reads.
notes: Reset mode is discouraged by the manual and unsupported by ttsim; it may produce nondeterministic hangs.

55.name: SETRWC

fields.name: clear_ab_vld
fields.meaning: Source-bank release mask: 0 keeps both, 1 flips/releases SrcA, 2 SrcB, 3 both. Release hands the consumed bank back to the unpacker unless clearing is disabled in configuration.

fields.name: rwc_cr
fields.meaning: Carry/reset controls: 1 SrcA, 2 SrcB, 4 Dst; 8 adds the current Dst counter rather than its carry/reset copy when setting Dst.

fields.name: rwc_d
fields.meaning: New Dst counter contribution (four bits).

fields.name: rwc_b
fields.meaning: New SrcB counter contribution (four bits).

fields.name: rwc_a
fields.meaning: New SrcA counter contribution (four bits).

fields.name: BitMask
fields.meaning: Update mask: 1 SrcA, 2 SrcB, 4 Dst, 8 reset fidelity to zero. 15 resets all with zero counter operands.

55.title: Set math read/write counters
55.summary: Set selected SrcA, SrcB and Dst counters, optionally reset fidelity, and optionally release source banks.
notes: rwc_cr changes whether values are relative to saved carry/reset counters. BitMask determines which counters actually change. Zero-valued arguments do not reset a counter whose mask bit is clear.

56.name: INCRWC

fields.name: rwc_cr
fields.meaning: 1 increments SrcA carry/reset then copies to SrcA; 2 similarly for SrcB; 4 similarly for Dst. With a bit clear only the running counter advances. Keep unsupported high bits zero.

fields.name: rwc_d
fields.meaning: Unsigned four-bit Dst increment.

fields.name: rwc_b
fields.meaning: Unsigned four-bit SrcB increment.

fields.name: rwc_a
fields.meaning: Unsigned four-bit SrcA increment.

56.title: Increment math read/write counters
56.summary: Advance SrcA, SrcB and Dst read/write counters without issuing arithmetic.
notes: Llama uses TTINCRWC(0, 2, 0, 0) to advance the Dst selection between even/odd vector chunks. This is a row-address counter operation, not a byte-pointer increment.

65.name: PACR

fields.name: CfgContext
fields.meaning: Keep zero for the documented operation. The Python encoder exposes these bits, but they are not an independent supported operand in the reference syntax.

fields.name: RowPadZero
fields.meaning: Keep zero for the documented operation. The Python encoder exposes these bits, but they are not an independent supported operand in the reference syntax.

fields.name: DstAccessMode
fields.meaning: Keep zero for the documented operation. The Python encoder exposes these bits, but they are not an independent supported operand in the reference syntax.

fields.name: AddrMode
fields.meaning: Select a configured packer ADC address-modifier slot (0-3) for the following pack operation.

fields.name: AddrCntContext
fields.meaning: Keep zero for the documented operation. The Python encoder exposes these bits, but they are not an independent supported operand in the reference syntax.

fields.name: ZeroWrite
fields.meaning: 1 uses zero input instead of reading Dst.

fields.name: ReadIntfSel
fields.meaning: Packer mask: 0 or 1 selects packer 0; 2, 4, 8 select one other packer; 3 selects 0+1; 12 selects 2+3; 15 selects all. Other combinations are not generally supported.

fields.name: OvrdThreadId
fields.meaning: Overrides the ADC thread selection; leave 0 for the ordinary current-thread path.

fields.name: Concat
fields.meaning: Compression-row continuation control. Only the documented Concat bit is meaningful; normal uncompressed packing uses 0.

fields.name: CtxtCtrl
fields.meaning: Keep zero for the documented operation. The Python encoder exposes these bits, but they are not an independent supported operand in the reference syntax.

fields.name: Flush
fields.meaning: Flush output buffers without fetching new input datums; reset output-address state for the next command.

fields.name: Last
fields.meaning: Flush the output after this pack and start fresh output addresses on the next PACR.

65.title: Pack Dst into L1
65.summary: Issue work to the configured packers, converting Dst values to an output format and writing the result to L1.
notes: Output address, format, count, strides, activation and rounding come from configuration and ADC state, not these instruction arguments.
Several legacy fields in the Python signature are absent from the shared public syntax. Repository calls keep them zero. Do not infer supported padding or context functionality from their names.
The Last bit finalizes the packer stream; it is not a cross-unit memory barrier. Use the repository's completion synchronization before publishing or reusing buffers.

66.name: UNPACR

fields.name: Unpack_block_selection
fields.meaning: 0 selects unpacker 0 (SrcA or direct Dst); 1 selects unpacker 1 (SrcB).

fields.name: AddrMode
fields.meaning: Four two-bit increments: bits 7:6 Ch1 Y, 5:4 Ch1 Z, 3:2 Ch0 Y, 1:0 Ch0 Z. Applied for the next unpack operation.

fields.name: CfgContextCntInc
fields.meaning: Keep 0 for a regular unpack. Nonzero values select the separate context-counter command form.

fields.name: CfgContextId
fields.meaning: Configuration context number when explicit multi-context selection is active.

fields.name: AddrCntContextId
fields.meaning: Address-counter context selector in multi-context mode. Regular repository calls use 0.

fields.name: OvrdThreadId
fields.meaning: Selects multi-context behavior in the reference model; the legacy argument name is misleading. Repository regular calls use 1.

fields.name: SetDatValid
fields.meaning: 1 gives the filled source bank to math and flips the unpacker bank. Direct-to-Dst calls handle synchronization separately.

fields.name: srcb_bcast
fields.meaning: Keep 0 for the regular unpack form. This bit is not ordinary FPU SrcB broadcasting.

fields.name: ZeroWrite2
fields.meaning: 1 replaces unpacked datums with zero.

fields.name: AutoIncContextID
fields.meaning: Use/increment the configured context counter rather than only the immediate context selector.

fields.name: RowSearch
fields.meaning: Select row-search addressing. Repository regular calls keep 0.

fields.name: SearchCacheFlush
fields.meaning: Selects the separate decompression-cache flush command. Keep 0 for ordinary unpack.

fields.name: Last
fields.meaning: Keep 0 for the regular unpack form; this is not the packer Last bit.

66.title: Unpack L1 into source or destination registers
66.summary: Issue work to unpacker 0 or 1. Configuration supplies formats, base addresses, tensor dimensions and the output interface.
notes: Unpacker 0 can write Dst directly, but doing so clobbers its SrcA bank. It still waits on SrcA ownership. Unpacker 1 cannot perform this direct-to-Dst path.
ADC counters and format configuration determine actual data movement. A bare TTUNPACR does not include a pointer or byte count.
The shared manual includes explicit Blackhole branches for 32-element unpack rows and throttle behavior. Some multi-context and compressed modes are not fully characterized.

67.name: UNPACR_NOP

fields.name: Unpacker_Select
fields.meaning: 0 selects unpacker 0; 1 selects unpacker 1.

fields.name: Stream_Id
fields.meaning: Stream identifier for the overlay-clear variant; zero for bank publication.

fields.name: Msg_Clr_Cnt
fields.meaning: Message clear count for the overlay-clear variant; zero for bank publication.

fields.name: Set_Dvalid
fields.meaning: Dvalid control. Repository SrcB publication uses 1 with Unpack_Pop=1.

fields.name: Clr_to1_fmt_Ctrl
fields.meaning: Format control for the source-clear variant; keep 0 for bank publication.

fields.name: Stall_Clr_Cntrl
fields.meaning: Stall-clear control for variant-specific behavior; keep 0 for bank publication.

fields.name: Bank_Clr_Ctrl
fields.meaning: Bank-clear control for source clearing; keep 0 for bank publication.

fields.name: Src_ClrVal_Ctrl
fields.meaning: Source fill selector for the source-clear variant; keep 0 for bank publication.

fields.name: Unpack_Pop
fields.meaning: Selects command behavior together with the other control bits. Repository publication uses 1.

67.title: Unpacker-sequenced control
67.summary: Perform an action ordered with unpacking: publish a source bank, clear sources, write selected registers, or occupy an unpacker cycle.
notes: This is not necessarily a no-op: the repository uses TTUNPACR_NOP(1, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1) to give SrcB to math.
The public reference defines separate command forms. The full cross-product of legacy field values is not documented; consult the specific form before changing the publication recipe.

69.name: SETDMAREG

fields.name: Payload_SigSelSize
fields.meaning: For immediate writes, this field carries the high two payload bits in the legacy split encoding. Zero with a small immediate.

fields.name: Payload_SigSel
fields.meaning: Low 14 bits of the immediate payload. The complete immediate spans encoder bits 23:8 together with Payload_SigSelSize.

fields.name: SetSignalsMode
fields.meaning: 0 selects immediate half-register writes. Special signal reads use a different command mode.

fields.name: RegIndex16b
fields.meaning: Half-register index: even selects low 16 bits, odd selects high 16 bits of GPR[index // 2].

69.title: Set a Tensix GPR half-word
69.summary: Write 16 immediate bits into one half of a Tensix GPR, preserving the other half.
notes: This is the scalar Tensix GPR file, not the SFPU LRegs and not RV32 registers. The repository can fill the immediate field dynamically by combining a base word with shifted bits.

80.name: SETADC

fields.name: CntSetMask
fields.meaning: Unit mask: 1 unpacker 0, 2 unpacker 1, 4 packers; OR bits to update multiple units.

fields.name: ChannelIndex
fields.meaning: Address-generator channel: 0 or 1.

fields.name: DimensionIndex
fields.meaning: Dimension selector: 0 X, 1 Y, 2 Z, 3 W.

fields.name: Value
fields.meaning: New counter value. The high bits can encode a thread override; ordinary use keeps those zero.

80.title: Set an address counter
80.summary: Assign one selected X/Y/Z/W counter and its carry/reset value for the chosen unit(s).
notes: Counter units depend on the configured address generator. They are not universally bytes: packer Y/Z/W can address rows, faces and tiles.

81.name: SETADCXY

fields.name: CntSetMask
fields.meaning: Unit mask: 1 unpacker 0, 2 unpacker 1, 4 packers; OR bits to update multiple units.

fields.name: Ch1_Y
fields.meaning: New channel 1 Y value; documented semantic value is three bits. Upper encoder bits are not ordinary counter payload.

fields.name: Ch1_X
fields.meaning: New channel 1 X value (three bits).

fields.name: Ch0_Y
fields.meaning: New channel 0 Y value (three bits).

fields.name: Ch0_X
fields.meaning: New channel 0 X value (three bits).

fields.name: BitMask
fields.meaning: Update mask: 1 Ch0 X, 2 Ch0 Y, 4 Ch1 X, 8 Ch1 Y; 15 updates all four. Upper encoder bits are not ordinary mask bits.

81.title: Set X/Y address counters
81.summary: Assign selected channel 0 and 1 X/Y counters and their carry/reset copies.

84.name: SETADCZW

fields.name: CntSetMask
fields.meaning: Unit mask: 1 unpacker 0, 2 unpacker 1, 4 packers; OR bits to update multiple units.

fields.name: Ch1_W
fields.meaning: New channel 1 W value; documented semantic value is three bits. Upper encoder bits are not ordinary counter payload.

fields.name: Ch1_Z
fields.meaning: New channel 1 Z value (three bits).

fields.name: Ch0_W
fields.meaning: New channel 0 W value (three bits).

fields.name: Ch0_Z
fields.meaning: New channel 0 Z value (three bits).

fields.name: BitMask
fields.meaning: Update mask: 1 Ch0 Z, 2 Ch0 W, 4 Ch1 Z, 8 Ch1 W; 15 updates all four. Upper encoder bits are not ordinary mask bits.

84.title: Set Z/W address counters
84.summary: Assign selected channel 0 and 1 Z/W counters and their carry/reset copies.

94.name: SETADCXX

fields.name: CntSetMask
fields.meaning: Unit mask: 1 unpacker 0, 2 unpacker 1, 4 packers; OR bits to update multiple units.

fields.name: x_end2
fields.meaning: Channel 1 X. In the repository's regular unpack/pack setup this is the inclusive end (element count minus one). The semantic value is 10 bits despite the wider Python field.

fields.name: x_start
fields.meaning: Channel 0 X start value (10 bits).

94.title: Set both X counters
94.summary: Set channel 0 X and channel 1 X for selected unpackers or packers.
notes: For 16 datums starting at zero, the repository uses x_end2=15 and x_start=0. Both counters' carry/reset copies are updated.

96.name: DMANOP
96.title: Scalar/DMA no operation
96.summary: Issue a no-op on the scalar/DMA path.
notes: Used near configuration and packing setup. A no-op is not a replacement for waiting for outstanding DMA or pack work.

112.name: SFPLOAD

fields.name: lreg_ind
fields.meaning: Destination LReg index. Loads write L0-L7.

fields.name: instr_mod0
fields.meaning: Transfer format: 0 follows configured format, 1 FP16, 2 BF16, 3 FP32. Integer and partial-word modes have distinct meanings; see the mode constants and ISA reference. This is not the same mode numbering as SFPLOADI.

fields.name: sfpu_addr_mode
fields.meaning: Raw SFPU address-modifier field, applied after the transfer. It advances SrcA/SrcB/Dst counters, not fidelity. Llama uses 7 with its configured counters. Do not interpret this as a byte increment.

fields.name: dest_reg_addr
fields.meaning: Dst address immediate plus configured offsets and RWCs. For normal addressing, the effective low 10 bits select four rows (bits 9:2) and even/odd columns (bit 1); bit 0 is unused. Keep reserved upper bits zero.

112.title: Load Dst into a vector register
112.summary: Read up to 32 values from Dst into one SFPU register, converting from the selected Dst storage format.
notes: One vector covers even or odd columns of four consecutive 16-column Dst rows. Lane n reads row (address & ~3) + n//8 and column 2*(n%8), plus the odd-column selection. Lane configuration can block or exchange columns.
An FPU write to the same Dst region needs at least three unrelated Tensix instructions before SFPLOAD. ZEROACC alone does not establish valid values for an SFPU load.

113.name: SFPLOADI

fields.name: lreg_ind
fields.meaning: Destination register L0-L7.

fields.name: instr_mod0
fields.meaning: 0: BF16 bits shifted into the high half; 1: FP16-like conversion; 2: zero-extended uint16; 4: sign-extended int16; 8: replace upper 16 bits; 10: replace lower 16 bits.

fields.name: imm16
fields.meaning: 16-bit bit pattern, not a Python float. Modes 8 and 10 preserve the opposite half.

113.title: Load an immediate into a vector register
113.summary: Broadcast a 16-bit immediate to active lanes, either converting it to 32 bits or replacing half of each register value.
notes: Llama installs exact FP32 constants with LOWER (10) followed by UPPER (8). For pi, the two immediates are 0x0fdb and 0x4049. Both writes obey lane predication.

114.name: SFPSTORE

fields.name: lreg_ind
fields.meaning: Source LReg index. Normal data registers are L0-L7; constants can also be read.

fields.name: instr_mod0
fields.meaning: Transfer format: 0 follows configured format, 1 FP16, 2 BF16, 3 FP32. Integer and partial-word modes have distinct meanings; see the mode constants and ISA reference. This is not the same mode numbering as SFPLOADI.

fields.name: sfpu_addr_mode
fields.meaning: Raw SFPU address-modifier field, applied after the transfer. It advances SrcA/SrcB/Dst counters, not fidelity. Llama uses 7 with its configured counters. Do not interpret this as a byte increment.

fields.name: dest_reg_addr
fields.meaning: Dst address immediate plus configured offsets and RWCs. For normal addressing, the effective low 10 bits select four rows (bits 9:2) and even/odd columns (bit 1); bit 0 is unused. Keep reserved upper bits zero.

114.title: Store a vector register into Dst
114.summary: Write active SFPU lanes into Dst with the selected format conversion. This does not write L1; packing is a separate step.
notes: Normal lane mapping is the inverse of SFPLOAD. An SFPU register is 32 lanes arranged as four groups of eight, not one contiguous tensor row.
Writing only part of an undefined Dst row is not a valid way to initialize it. Initialize the row before a partial or predicated store.

116.name: SFPMULI

fields.name: imm16_math
fields.meaning: BF16 immediate bit pattern, widened to FP32 by shifting left 16 bits. Not an integer numerical value.

fields.name: lreg_dest
fields.meaning: LReg index used as both input and output.

fields.name: instr_mod1
fields.meaning: Blackhole flags: 1 negates A, 2 negates C, 4 takes A index from L7 low four bits, 8 takes destination index from L7. Combine flags with bitwise OR; 0 is ordinary arithmetic.

116.title: Floating-point multiply with an immediate
116.summary: Convert a BF16 immediate to FP32 and multiply it with the old destination in each active lane.
notes: Blackhole MAD has a two-cycle result latency and usually stalls direct dependencies automatically. Load-macro sequences and some consumers (including SFPIADD, SFPSHFT, SFPSWAP and SFPSHFT2 modes) need explicit spacing. Llama commonly inserts TTSFPNOP.

117.name: SFPADDI

fields.name: imm16_math
fields.meaning: BF16 immediate bit pattern, widened to FP32 by shifting left 16 bits. Not an integer numerical value.

fields.name: lreg_dest
fields.meaning: LReg index used as both input and output.

fields.name: instr_mod1
fields.meaning: Blackhole flags: 1 negates A, 2 negates C, 4 takes A index from L7 low four bits, 8 takes destination index from L7. Combine flags with bitwise OR; 0 is ordinary arithmetic.

117.title: Floating-point add with an immediate
117.summary: Convert a BF16 immediate to FP32 and add it with the old destination in each active lane.
notes: Blackhole MAD has a two-cycle result latency and usually stalls direct dependencies automatically. Load-macro sequences and some consumers (including SFPIADD, SFPSHFT, SFPSWAP and SFPSHFT2 modes) need explicit spacing. Llama commonly inserts TTSFPNOP.

119.name: SFPEXEXP

fields.name: imm12_math
fields.meaning: Keep zero for the documented operation. The Python encoder exposes these bits, but they are not an independent supported operand in the reference syntax.

fields.name: lreg_c
fields.meaning: Source vector register index (VC). L0-L7 are writable vectors; higher indices select constants or special registers.

fields.name: lreg_dest
fields.meaning: Destination vector register index (VD). Normal arithmetic writes L0-L7. Destinations 12-15 can record instruction templates when backdoor loading is enabled.

fields.name: instr_mod1
fields.meaning: 0 extracts exponent minus 127; OR 1 to keep the bias; OR 2 to set flags from the result sign; OR 8 to invert that condition.

119.title: Extract a floating-point exponent
119.summary: Extract the FP32 exponent bits into an integer vector, optionally removing the exponent bias.
notes: This manipulates the representation rather than evaluating log, exp or a general transcendental function. Exact modifiers are listed in the source reference.

120.name: SFPEXMAN

fields.name: imm12_math
fields.meaning: Keep zero for the documented operation. The Python encoder exposes these bits, but they are not an independent supported operand in the reference syntax.

fields.name: lreg_c
fields.meaning: Source vector register index (VC). L0-L7 are writable vectors; higher indices select constants or special registers.

fields.name: lreg_dest
fields.meaning: Destination vector register index (VD). Normal arithmetic writes L0-L7. Destinations 12-15 can record instruction templates when backdoor loading is enabled.

fields.name: instr_mod1
fields.meaning: 0 includes a 1 in bit 23 (hidden leading bit); 1 leaves bit 23 zero. The upper eight output bits are zero.

120.title: Extract a floating-point mantissa
120.summary: Extract the low 23 mantissa bits into an integer, optionally setting bit 23 to represent the hidden leading bit.
notes: This manipulates the representation rather than evaluating log, exp or a general transcendental function. Exact modifiers are listed in the source reference.

121.name: SFPIADD

fields.name: imm12_math
fields.meaning: Signed 12-bit immediate encoded as value & 0xfff, used when modifier bit 0 is set.

fields.name: lreg_c
fields.meaning: Source vector register index (VC). L0-L7 are writable vectors; higher indices select constants or special registers.

fields.name: lreg_dest
fields.meaning: Destination and, in register mode, the second source operand. Subtraction is VC - old VD.

fields.name: instr_mod1
fields.meaning: 1 selects immediate addition; 2 selects VC - VD; otherwise VC + VD. OR 4 to preserve condition flags. Without 4, flags reflect a negative result; 8 inverts the condition.

121.title: Integer add or subtract
121.summary: Perform 32-bit integer arithmetic on register bit patterns, optionally updating per-lane condition flags.
notes: Llama uses modifier 6 (2 | 4) to subtract the shifted FP32 bit pattern from an inverse-square-root seed without changing lane flags.

Blackhole MAD has a two-cycle result latency and usually stalls direct dependencies automatically. Load-macro sequences and some consumers (including SFPIADD, SFPSHFT, SFPSWAP and SFPSHFT2 modes) need explicit spacing. Llama commonly inserts TTSFPNOP.

122.name: SFPSHFT

fields.name: imm12_math
fields.meaning: Signed shift amount encoded in 12 bits when modifier 1 is used. Positive shifts left; negative shifts right.

fields.name: lreg_c
fields.meaning: Register supplying the shift amount when immediate mode is disabled.

fields.name: lreg_dest
fields.meaning: Register holding the data to shift, overwritten with the result.

fields.name: instr_mod1
fields.meaning: 1 selects immediate shift amount; 0 selects the register shift amount.

122.title: Shift integer bits within each lane
122.summary: Shift the old destination left or logically right. This changes bits inside each lane; it does not move data between lanes.
notes: Llama uses imm12_math=0xfff (-1), modifier 1 to shift a positive FP32 bit representation right by one for rsqrt estimation.

123.name: SFPSETCC

fields.name: imm12_math
fields.meaning: Low immediate bit supplies the condition in immediate mode; zero for register comparisons.

fields.name: lreg_c
fields.meaning: Source vector register index (VC). L0-L7 are writable vectors; higher indices select constants or special registers.

fields.name: lreg_dest
fields.meaning: Normally zero; not the destination of a vector arithmetic result.

fields.name: instr_mod1
fields.meaning: 0 tests sign/negative, 2 nonzero, 4 nonnegative, 6 zero; 1 selects immediate bit 0; 8 clears flags. Conditions update lane flags as specified by the functional model.

123.title: Set per-lane condition flags
123.summary: Update per-lane flags from the sign or zero status of a register or an immediate condition.
notes: SFPENCC controls whether these flags gate instruction execution. This writes predication state, not a vector of integer booleans.

124.name: SFPMOV

fields.name: imm12_math
fields.meaning: Keep zero for the documented operation. The Python encoder exposes these bits, but they are not an independent supported operand in the reference syntax.

fields.name: lreg_c
fields.meaning: Source vector register index (VC). L0-L7 are writable vectors; higher indices select constants or special registers.

fields.name: lreg_dest
fields.meaning: Destination vector register index (VD). Normal arithmetic writes L0-L7. Destinations 12-15 can record instruction templates when backdoor loading is enabled.

fields.name: instr_mod1
fields.meaning: 0 copies VC to VD; 1 toggles the FP32/sign-magnitude sign bit; 2 copies with all lanes enabled; 8 reads special state selected by VC.

124.title: Copy or negate a vector
124.summary: Copy a register, toggle its sign bit, bypass predication, or read special SFPU state.
notes: Negation flips bit 31. It is not two's-complement integer negation. In special mode, VC=9 advances the hardware PRNG.

125.name: SFPABS

fields.name: imm12_math
fields.meaning: Keep zero for the documented operation. The Python encoder exposes these bits, but they are not an independent supported operand in the reference syntax.

fields.name: lreg_c
fields.meaning: Source vector register index (VC). L0-L7 are writable vectors; higher indices select constants or special registers.

fields.name: lreg_dest
fields.meaning: Destination vector register index (VD). Normal arithmetic writes L0-L7. Destinations 12-15 can record instruction templates when backdoor loading is enabled.

fields.name: instr_mod1
fields.meaning: 0 selects two’s-complement integer absolute value; 1 selects FP32.

125.title: Vector absolute value
125.summary: Take the lanewise absolute value of two’s-complement integers or FP32 values.
notes: FP32 negative NaNs retain their sign. Integer -2147483648 is unchanged.

126.name: SFPAND

fields.name: imm12_math
fields.meaning: Blackhole VB selector occupies the low four bits of this raw 12-bit encoder field; keep the upper bits zero.

fields.name: lreg_c
fields.meaning: Source vector register index (VC). L0-L7 are writable vectors; higher indices select constants or special registers.

fields.name: lreg_dest
fields.meaning: Destination vector register index (VD). Normal arithmetic writes L0-L7. Destinations 12-15 can record instruction templates when backdoor loading is enabled.

fields.name: instr_mod1
fields.meaning: Bit 0 selects VB as the first input. When clear, the destination register is also the first input.

126.title: Vector bitwise AND
126.summary: Apply bitwise AND to each pair of 32-bit lanes.
notes: VB selection is a Blackhole extension; the Wormhole two-input form always reuses VD.

127.name: SFPOR

fields.name: imm12_math
fields.meaning: Blackhole VB selector occupies the low four bits of this raw 12-bit encoder field; keep the upper bits zero.

fields.name: lreg_c
fields.meaning: Source vector register index (VC). L0-L7 are writable vectors; higher indices select constants or special registers.

fields.name: lreg_dest
fields.meaning: Destination vector register index (VD). Normal arithmetic writes L0-L7. Destinations 12-15 can record instruction templates when backdoor loading is enabled.

fields.name: instr_mod1
fields.meaning: Bit 0 selects VB as the first input. When clear, the destination register is also the first input.

127.title: Vector bitwise OR
127.summary: Apply bitwise OR to each pair of 32-bit lanes.
notes: VB selection is a Blackhole extension; the Wormhole two-input form always reuses VD.

130.name: SFPSETEXP

fields.name: imm12_math
fields.meaning: Unsigned eight-bit biased exponent in immediate mode. Keep the remaining encoder bits zero.

fields.name: lreg_c
fields.meaning: Source vector register index (VC). L0-L7 are writable vectors; higher indices select constants or special registers.

fields.name: lreg_dest
fields.meaning: Destination vector register index (VD). Normal arithmetic writes L0-L7. Destinations 12-15 can record instruction templates when backdoor loading is enabled.

fields.name: instr_mod1
fields.meaning: 1 selects the immediate exponent; otherwise take bits from old VD. With register input, OR 2 takes VD exponent bits 30:23 instead of its low eight integer bits.

130.title: Replace a floating-point exponent
130.summary: Replace the source exponent using immediate or destination-register bits, preserving source sign and mantissa.
notes: This manipulates the representation rather than evaluating log, exp or a general transcendental function. Exact modifiers are listed in the source reference.

132.name: SFPMAD

fields.name: lreg_src_a
fields.meaning: A register index. For SFPADD use L10, the 1.0 constant; ordinary register indices are four bits despite this eight-bit encoder field.

fields.name: lreg_src_b
fields.meaning: B register index.

fields.name: lreg_src_c
fields.meaning: C register index. For SFPMUL use L9, the 0.0 constant.

fields.name: lreg_dest
fields.meaning: Destination vector register index (VD). Normal arithmetic writes L0-L7. Destinations 12-15 can record instruction templates when backdoor loading is enabled.

fields.name: instr_mod1
fields.meaning: Blackhole flags: 1 negates A, 2 negates C, 4 takes A index from L7 low four bits, 8 takes destination index from L7. Combine flags with bitwise OR; 0 is ordinary arithmetic.

132.title: Multiply then add
132.summary: Compute VD = A * B + C independently in each active FP32 lane, with optional sign and indirect-register modifiers.
notes: Blackhole MAD has a two-cycle result latency and usually stalls direct dependencies automatically. Load-macro sequences and some consumers (including SFPIADD, SFPSHFT, SFPSWAP and SFPSHFT2 modes) need explicit spacing. Llama commonly inserts TTSFPNOP.
Multiply-add is partially fused, not an exact IEEE fused multiply-add. Denormal inputs are treated as zero and denormal outputs flush to signed zero; Blackhole uses round-to-nearest, ties-to-even.

133.name: SFPADD

fields.name: lreg_src_a
fields.meaning: A register index. For SFPADD use L10, the 1.0 constant; ordinary register indices are four bits despite this eight-bit encoder field.

fields.name: lreg_src_b
fields.meaning: B register index.

fields.name: lreg_src_c
fields.meaning: C register index. For SFPMUL use L9, the 0.0 constant.

fields.name: lreg_dest
fields.meaning: Destination vector register index (VD). Normal arithmetic writes L0-L7. Destinations 12-15 can record instruction templates when backdoor loading is enabled.

fields.name: instr_mod1
fields.meaning: Blackhole flags: 1 negates A, 2 negates C, 4 takes A index from L7 low four bits, 8 takes destination index from L7. Combine flags with bitwise OR; 0 is ordinary arithmetic.

133.title: Floating-point add or subtract
133.summary: Compute VD = B + C using the MAD datapath with A fixed to L10 (1.0).
notes: Blackhole MAD has a two-cycle result latency and usually stalls direct dependencies automatically. Load-macro sequences and some consumers (including SFPIADD, SFPSHFT, SFPSWAP and SFPSHFT2 modes) need explicit spacing. Llama commonly inserts TTSFPNOP.
Multiply-add is partially fused, not an exact IEEE fused multiply-add. Denormal inputs are treated as zero and denormal outputs flush to signed zero; Blackhole uses round-to-nearest, ties-to-even.

134.name: SFPMUL

fields.name: lreg_src_a
fields.meaning: A register index. For SFPADD use L10, the 1.0 constant; ordinary register indices are four bits despite this eight-bit encoder field.

fields.name: lreg_src_b
fields.meaning: B register index.

fields.name: lreg_src_c
fields.meaning: C register index. For SFPMUL use L9, the 0.0 constant.

fields.name: lreg_dest
fields.meaning: Destination vector register index (VD). Normal arithmetic writes L0-L7. Destinations 12-15 can record instruction templates when backdoor loading is enabled.

fields.name: instr_mod1
fields.meaning: Blackhole flags: 1 negates A, 2 negates C, 4 takes A index from L7 low four bits, 8 takes destination index from L7. Combine flags with bitwise OR; 0 is ordinary arithmetic.

134.title: Floating-point multiply
134.summary: Compute VD = A * B using the MAD datapath with C fixed to L9 (0.0).
notes: Blackhole MAD has a two-cycle result latency and usually stalls direct dependencies automatically. Load-macro sequences and some consumers (including SFPIADD, SFPSHFT, SFPSWAP and SFPSHFT2 modes) need explicit spacing. Llama commonly inserts TTSFPNOP.
Multiply-add is partially fused, not an exact IEEE fused multiply-add. Denormal inputs are treated as zero and denormal outputs flush to signed zero; Blackhole uses round-to-nearest, ties-to-even.

135.name: SFPPUSHC

fields.name: imm12_math
fields.meaning: Keep zero for the documented operation. The Python encoder exposes these bits, but they are not an independent supported operand in the reference syntax.

fields.name: lreg_c
fields.meaning: Keep zero for the documented operation. The Python encoder exposes these bits, but they are not an independent supported operand in the reference syntax.

fields.name: lreg_dest
fields.meaning: Normally zero; not a data-register output.

fields.name: instr_mod1
fields.meaning: Keep zero. Pushes lane flags and the predicate-enable state onto the eight-entry conditional stack; do not overflow it.

135.title: Push conditional state
135.summary: Save or restore the SFPU per-lane conditional-execution state using the predicate stack.
notes: Useful for nested predication. This is a predicate stack, not a Dst data spill or the RV32 call stack.

136.name: SFPPOPC

fields.name: imm12_math
fields.meaning: Keep zero for the documented operation. The Python encoder exposes these bits, but they are not an independent supported operand in the reference syntax.

fields.name: lreg_c
fields.meaning: Keep zero for the documented operation. The Python encoder exposes these bits, but they are not an independent supported operand in the reference syntax.

fields.name: lreg_dest
fields.meaning: Normally zero; not a data-register output.

fields.name: instr_mod1
fields.meaning: 0 pops and restores both flags and predicate enable; 1-12 peek and combine flags with stack-top flags; 13 inverts flags; 14 enables predication with true flags; 15 enables it with false flags. Do not pop an empty stack or use peek modes on a full stack.

136.title: Pop conditional state
136.summary: Save or restore the SFPU per-lane conditional-execution state using the predicate stack.
notes: Useful for nested predication. This is a predicate stack, not a Dst data spill or the RV32 call stack.

138.name: SFPENCC

fields.name: imm12_math
fields.meaning: Low bit selects whether lane flags are used for enable; bit 1 supplies a new flag value when requested by Mod1.

fields.name: lreg_c
fields.meaning: Keep zero for the documented operation. The Python encoder exposes these bits, but they are not an independent supported operand in the reference syntax.

fields.name: lreg_dest
fields.meaning: Normally zero; only relevant to backdoor instruction recording.

fields.name: instr_mod1
fields.meaning: 1 toggles predicate use; 2 assigns predicate use from immediate bit 0; 8 assigns flags from immediate bit 1. If 8 is absent, flags become true.

138.title: Enable or reset lane predication
138.summary: Control whether per-lane flags gate subsequent SFPU instructions, and reset the flags.
notes: This configures predication, not a floating-point comparison. Restore all-lane behavior explicitly after a predicated region.

140.name: SFPTRANSP

fields.name: imm12_math
fields.meaning: Keep zero for the documented operation. The Python encoder exposes these bits, but they are not an independent supported operand in the reference syntax.

fields.name: lreg_c
fields.meaning: Keep zero for the documented operation. The Python encoder exposes these bits, but they are not an independent supported operand in the reference syntax.

fields.name: lreg_dest
fields.meaning: Normally zero. This field gates backdoor-template behavior; it does not select a single output register.

fields.name: instr_mod1
fields.meaning: Keep zero for the documented operation. The Python encoder exposes these bits, but they are not an independent supported operand in the reference syntax.

140.title: Transpose between vector registers
140.summary: Transpose the register axis and four-row lane-group axis for both L0-L3 and L4-L7.
notes: Treat each group of four registers as a 4 x 4 x 8 array. This swaps the first two axes, preserving the eight-column axis. It is not a 4 x 8 tensor transpose. Both register groups are affected.

141.name: SFPXOR

fields.name: imm12_math
fields.meaning: Keep zero for the documented operation. The Python encoder exposes these bits, but they are not an independent supported operand in the reference syntax.

fields.name: lreg_c
fields.meaning: Source vector register index (VC). L0-L7 are writable vectors; higher indices select constants or special registers.

fields.name: lreg_dest
fields.meaning: Destination vector register index (VD). Normal arithmetic writes L0-L7. Destinations 12-15 can record instruction templates when backdoor loading is enabled.

fields.name: instr_mod1
fields.meaning: Keep zero for the documented operation. The Python encoder exposes these bits, but they are not an independent supported operand in the reference syntax.

141.title: Vector bitwise XOR
141.summary: XOR each destination lane with the corresponding VC lane.
notes: The destination is both input and output.

143.name: SFPNOP
143.title: SFPU no operation
143.summary: Occupy an SFPU instruction slot without changing arithmetic data.
notes: Useful for explicit SFPU dependency spacing, including cases missed by Blackhole automatic stalls. It is not a global completion barrier.

144.name: SFPCAST

fields.name: lreg_src_c
fields.meaning: Source vector register index (VC). L0-L7 are writable vectors; higher indices select constants or special registers.

fields.name: lreg_dest
fields.meaning: Destination vector register index (VD). Normal arithmetic writes L0-L7. Destinations 12-15 can record instruction templates when backdoor loading is enabled.

fields.name: instr_mod1
fields.meaning: 0 converts sign-magnitude int32 to FP32 with nearest-even rounding; 1 uses stochastic rounding; 2 computes two's-complement absolute value (prefer SFPABS); 3 converts between two's-complement and sign-magnitude.

144.title: Convert integer representations
144.summary: Convert sign-magnitude integers to FP32, convert between integer representations, or take integer absolute values.
notes: Some integer paths use sign-magnitude, others two's complement. A register bit-copy is not a numerical cast.

145.name: SFPCONFIG

fields.name: imm16_math
fields.meaning: Immediate value when modifier bit 0 is set, otherwise input normally comes from the first eight lanes of L0. With modifier bit 3 this supplies a lane mask.

fields.name: config_dest
fields.meaning: 0-3 instruction templates; 4-7 sequences; 8 miscellaneous macro control; 9 PRNG state; 11-14 programmable constants; 15 lane configuration. Consult the reference for destination-specific handling.

fields.name: instr_mod1
fields.meaning: 1 selects immediate input; 2 ORs, 4 ANDs, 6 XORs where supported; 8 applies the immediate lane mask. Templates require L0 because the instruction is 32 bits.

145.title: Configure SFPU lanes and load macros
145.summary: Write SFPU constant registers, lane configuration, instruction templates or load-macro sequences.
notes: Configuration input is sampled from the first eight lanes and replicated across four lane groups. Destination selection changes which operations and immediate forms are legal.
Llama records an arithmetic instruction with destination CONFIG0, then sets sequence 0 with config_dest=4 and miscellaneous control with config_dest=8.

146.name: SFPSWAP

fields.name: imm12_math
fields.meaning: Keep zero for the documented operation. The Python encoder exposes these bits, but they are not an independent supported operand in the reference syntax.

fields.name: lreg_src_c
fields.meaning: VC is both an input and an output. In mode 1 it receives the maximum.

fields.name: lreg_dest
fields.meaning: VD is both an input and an output. In mode 1 it receives the minimum.

fields.name: instr_mod1
fields.meaning: 0 swaps unconditionally; 1 gives VD=min, VC=max; 2-8 choose opposite min/max placement for different eight-lane subgroups; 9 gives VD=max, VC=min.

146.title: Swap or compare-exchange vectors
146.summary: Swap two registers, or compute a minimum and maximum simultaneously in each lane.
notes: Comparison ordering and special floating-point values follow the hardware model, not Python min/max. Both operands are modified. Additional argmin/argmax behavior depends on lane configuration.

147.name: SFPLOADMACRO

fields.name: lreg_ind
fields.meaning: Packed selector: high two bits select macro sequence 0-3; low two bits supply the low destination-register bits.

fields.name: instr_mod0
fields.meaning: Transfer format: 0 follows configured format, 1 FP16, 2 BF16, 3 FP32. Integer and partial-word modes have distinct meanings; see the mode constants and ISA reference. This is not the same mode numbering as SFPLOADI.

fields.name: sfpu_addr_mode
fields.meaning: Raw SFPU address-modifier field, applied after the transfer. It advances SrcA/SrcB/Dst counters, not fidelity. Llama uses 7 with its configured counters. Do not interpret this as a byte increment.

fields.name: dest_reg_addr
fields.meaning: Load address field. Its low bit participates in the macro destination selection; other address bits follow the load encoding. Use the SFPLOADMACRO-specific syntax, not an arbitrary SFPLOAD address.

147.title: Load and launch an SFPU sequence
147.summary: Perform a Dst load and schedule preconfigured simple, MAD, round and store operations behind it.
notes: Requires prior template, sequence and delay configuration. It can overlap SFPU subunits, unlike issuing one ordinary instruction per cycle.
Automatic dependency stalls do not protect instructions inside a macro. Program delays explicitly, including the two-cycle MAD result dependency.

148.name: SFPSHFT2

fields.name: imm12_math
fields.meaning: Mode-dependent VB register index or signed 12-bit immediate. Zero in Llama's lane-rotation mode.

fields.name: lreg_src_c
fields.meaning: Source vector VC for the single-vector shuffle modes.

fields.name: lreg_dest
fields.meaning: Destination vector register index (VD). Normal arithmetic writes L0-L7. Destinations 12-15 can record instruction templates when backdoor loading is enabled.

fields.name: instr_mod1
fields.meaning: 0 shifts L0-L3 register contents; 1 chained copy; 2 rotate-and-copy; 3 rotates right within each eight-lane group; 4 shifts right within each group with zero fill; 5 register-controlled bit shift; 6 immediate bit shift.

148.title: Shuffle lanes or shift bits
148.summary: Move values between lanes or perform per-lane shifts, depending on the selected mode.
notes: Mode 3 wraps lane 7 into lane 0 independently in each eight-lane group. Llama composes rotations, addition and SFPTRANSP to reduce across 32 lanes.
Blackhole fixes the zero-fill shuffle bug present in Wormhole. Some modes have dependency-stall exceptions; keep the explicit delay used in the kernels.

153.name: SFPARECIP

fields.name: imm12_math
fields.meaning: VB register index for conditional reciprocal; its signed integer sign decides whether to apply the reciprocal. Zero is sufficient in unconditional mode.

fields.name: lreg_c
fields.meaning: Source vector register index (VC). L0-L7 are writable vectors; higher indices select constants or special registers.

fields.name: lreg_dest
fields.meaning: Destination vector register index (VD). Normal arithmetic writes L0-L7. Destinations 12-15 can record instruction templates when backdoor loading is enabled.

fields.name: instr_mod1
fields.meaning: 0 reciprocal with sign preserved; 1 conditional reciprocal of the magnitude when VB is negative; 2 approximate exponential of the magnitude with the original sign reattached.

153.title: Approximate reciprocal or exponential
153.summary: Compute a Blackhole hardware reciprocal or restricted-range exponential estimate in each active lane.
notes: An estimate is a building block for refinement, not full-accuracy division. The reciprocal estimate of 1.0 is 0.99609375.

Exponential mode is useful for input magnitudes below 2. For negative inputs it returns a negative estimate of exp(abs(x)), not exp(x); a subsequent conditional reciprocal can be part of a composed exp sequence.

162.name: STALLWAIT

fields.name: stall_res
fields.meaning: Instruction-class bitmask. Repository bit numbers: 0 TDMA, 1 SYNC, 2 PACK, 3 UNPACK, 4 XMOV, 5 THCON, 6 MATH, 7 CFG, 8 SFPU. Set a bit using 1 << bit_number.

fields.name: wait_res
fields.meaning: Blackhole condition bitmask. Repository bit numbers: 0 THCON, 1 UNPACK0, 2 UNPACK1, 3 PACK0, 4 MATH, 5 SRCA_CLR, 6 SRCB_CLR, 7 SRCA_VLD, 8 SRCB_VLD, 9 XMOV, 10 TRISC_CFG, 11 SFPU, 12 CFGEXU. See the source condition table for the precise wait predicate.

162.title: Wait for selected hardware resources
162.summary: Latch conditions that block selected classes of subsequent instructions until the conditions clear.
notes: The issuing thread can continue until it reaches a blocked instruction class. This is not equivalent to immediately stopping every unit.
Resource-completion waits and semaphore waits have different conditions; do not substitute one for the other.

163.name: SEMINIT

fields.name: max_value
fields.meaning: Maximum semaphore value (four bits).

fields.name: init_value
fields.meaning: Initial semaphore value (four bits); choose a value within the configured maximum.

fields.name: sem_sel
fields.meaning: Semaphore bitmask, not an index.

163.title: Initialize semaphores
163.summary: Set the maximum and initial value of selected Tensix semaphores.
notes: Included as supporting reference even when initialization is emitted through other setup mechanisms.

164.name: SEMPOST

fields.name: sem_sel
fields.meaning: Semaphore bitmask, not index: use 1 << semaphore_number. The architecture has eight semaphore selectors despite the wider Python field.

164.title: Increment semaphore values
164.summary: Increment each selected Tensix semaphore value.
notes: Use SEMWAIT to test availability separately. Do not assume the GET/POST name implies a blocking wait or source-bank transfer.

165.name: SEMGET

fields.name: sem_sel
fields.meaning: Semaphore bitmask, not index: use 1 << semaphore_number. The architecture has eight semaphore selectors despite the wider Python field.

165.title: Decrement semaphore values
165.summary: Decrement each selected Tensix semaphore value.
notes: Use SEMWAIT to test availability separately. Do not assume the GET/POST name implies a blocking wait or source-bank transfer.

166.name: SEMWAIT

fields.name: stall_res
fields.meaning: Same instruction-class block mask as Blackhole STALLWAIT.

fields.name: sem_sel
fields.meaning: Semaphore bitmask: 1 << semaphore_number, or OR several bits.

fields.name: wait_sem_cond
fields.meaning: 1 waits while any selected semaphore is zero; 2 waits while any selected semaphore is at its maximum; 3 requires neither empty nor full. Zero is not a valid wait condition.

166.title: Wait on semaphore conditions
166.summary: Block selected instruction classes while selected semaphores are empty and/or full.
notes: This does not increment or decrement the semaphore. Combine it with GET or POST as required by the ownership protocol.

176.name: WRCFG

fields.name: GprAddress
fields.meaning: Source Tensix GPR index, not an RV32 register number.

fields.name: wr128b
fields.meaning: 0 writes one 32-bit word; 1 writes a 128-bit group. Respect group alignment for the wide form.

fields.name: CfgReg
fields.meaning: Backend configuration word index, not its byte address.

176.title: Write backend configuration from GPRs
176.summary: Copy Tensix GPR data into backend configuration registers.
notes: The packer setup uses TTWRCFG after writing the output destination into a Tensix GPR. Synchronize CPU-to-configuration visibility as required by the surrounding sequence.

177.name: RDCFG

fields.name: GprAddress
fields.meaning: Destination Tensix GPR index.

fields.name: CfgReg
fields.meaning: Backend configuration word index, not a byte address.

177.title: Read backend configuration into a GPR
177.summary: Copy a backend configuration value into a Tensix GPR.

178.name: SETC16

fields.name: setc16_reg
fields.meaning: Thread-configuration register index, not its byte MMIO address.

fields.name: setc16_value
fields.meaning: 16-bit immediate configuration value.

178.title: Write thread configuration
178.summary: Write a 16-bit immediate to a thread configuration register.
notes: SETC16 targets thread configuration. WRCFG and RMWCIB operate on a different configuration address space. The same integer index does not mean the same register across these instructions.

179.name: RMWCIB0

fields.name: Data
fields.meaning: New bits for the selected byte. Use values consistent with the mask.

fields.name: CfgRegAddr
fields.meaning: Backend configuration register index in the byte-immediate instruction's addressable range.

179.title: Update configuration byte 0
179.summary: Read-modify-write byte 0 of a backend configuration register using an immediate mask and data.
notes: These four opcodes choose which byte is changed. They do not take an additional byte-selector argument.
